options: A dedicated Salesforce edition with no other purpose
A regular org (production, Developer Edition, or trial) with a setting enabled that lets it create scratch orgs and second-generation packages
A type of sandbox specifically for packaging
A free tool installed separately from any Salesforce org
questions.explain: A Dev Hub is not a special edition — it's a regular production, Developer Edition, or trial org with the Dev Hub setting enabled, which unlocks scratch org creation and second-generation packaging.

questions.q: Which org type can NOT be enabled as a Dev Hub?
options: A production org
A Developer Edition org
A trial org
A sandbox
questions.explain: Sandboxes cannot be enabled as a Dev Hub — only production, Developer Edition, and trial orgs qualify.

questions.q: What happens if you enable Dev Hub on an org and later want to turn it back off?
options: You can disable it anytime from the same Setup page
You cannot disable it once enabled — it's a one-way switch
It automatically disables after 30 days
Only Salesforce Support can disable it, with no restrictions
questions.explain: Enabling Dev Hub is irreversible — once turned on, it cannot be disabled, which is why choosing the right org (ideally a stable production org for real use) matters.

questions.q: What risk does this lesson call out for using a trial or Developer Edition org as your Dev Hub for anything beyond short-term learning?
options: Trial orgs can never create scratch orgs at all
If the trial or Developer Edition org expires, you lose access to every package and scratch org allocation tied to it
Developer Edition orgs charge a hidden packaging fee
Trial orgs require a different CLI version
questions.explain: A trial or Developer Edition Dev Hub works for learning, but losing access to that org (through expiration) means losing access to everything tied to it — packages, scratch org allocations, all of it — which is why real team or ISV use favors an active production org.

questions.q: What does `sf config set target-dev-hub=DevHub` do?
options: Creates a brand-new Dev Hub org from scratch
Sets or changes which already-authenticated org the CLI treats as the default Dev Hub
Deletes the current default Dev Hub connection
Enables the Dev Hub setting inside the org's Setup menu remotely
questions.explain: sf config set target-dev-hub sets (or changes) which authenticated org alias the CLI uses by default whenever a command needs a Dev Hub, so you don't have to pass --target-dev-hub on every command.
